item.title: Shakira, Madonna, BTS, Justin Bieber & More Take Over FIFA’s First-Ever World Cup Final Halftime Show
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we're breaking down the most epic halftime show in FIFA World Cup history. I'm your host, and I'm here to take you through the wild ride that was the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final halftime show.
[Cut to music]
Host: The show kicked off with the one and only Madonna, making a grand entrance with DJ Stuart Price and Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho. But that was just the beginning. The show then transitioned to Gustavo Dudamel leading a dramatic take on "Seven Nation Army" with the New York Philharmonic and the Simón Bolívar Symphony Orchestra of Venezuela.
[Cut to sound effects: cheering crowd]
Host: Then, BTS took the stage in matching red, motorcycle-inspired outfits, performing a high-energy "Dynamite". Next up, Justin Bieber delivered a subdued acoustic performance of "Everything Hallelujah", introduced by Jason Sudeikis in his Ted Lasso persona.
[Cut to music]
Host: But the real stadium-pop peak came when Shakira and Burna Boy performed their hit song "Dai Dai", backed by the Ghetto Kids dancing. And just when you thought it was all over, the PS22 Chorus, Chris Martin, Kermit, Miss Piggy, and the rest of the cast came together for a grand finale, complete with a giant "LOVE" tableau and fireworks overhead.
[Cut to sound effects: cheering crowd, fireworks]
Host: It was a show that was undeniably memorable, but also slightly unhinged and deeply overstuffed. FIFA hoped to create a spectacle, and that's exactly what they got. Whether you loved it or hated it, the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final halftime show was an experience you won't soon forget.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more analysis and discussion on the world of sports and entertainment.
